notable.name: Catalan
notable.note: co-official in Catalonia, Valencia (as Valencian), and the Balearic Islands; bilingual signage common

notable.name: Basque (Euskara)
notable.family: Language isolate — not Indo-European, genuinely unique in Europe
notable.note: co-official in the Basque Country and Navarre; bilingual signage with a distinctive thick black border

notable.name: Galician
notable.note: co-official in Galicia, closely related to Portuguese

terrainDescription.zh: 中央為梅塞塔高原，四周環繞庇里牛斯山、坎塔布連山等山脈，地中海沿岸與南部安達魯西亞則屬典型地中海型氣候。
terrainDescription.en: A central Meseta plateau ringed by mountain ranges (Pyrenees, Cantabrian), with a classic Mediterranean climate along the coast and in the south (Andalusia).

plate.color: white background, black text, blue EU band with "E" on the left
plate.shape: rectangular, 500×110mm, format 1234 ABC (no vowels, no Ñ)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Wedge-shaped, often hollow, with an orange rectangular reflector on the front and two white circular reflectors on the back; some regional variation (e.g. Aragón, Asturias)

utilityPole.transformerMount: "Ladder" concrete poles with step-like indents common in small towns/rural areas; "French-style" upside-down-triangle poletops with a slightly upward-curved horizontal bar are also common, usually atop tall ladder poles or mid-size steel poles

historicalContext.zh: 西班牙全國官方語言為卡斯提亞語（西班牙語），但加泰隆尼亞語（加泰隆尼亞、瓦倫西亞、巴利亞利群島）、巴斯克語（非印歐語系的語言孤島）、加利西亞語（與葡萄牙語系出同源）在各自的自治區並列官方語言，路牌常見雙語並列，是辨識區域的強力線索。
historicalContext.en: Castilian Spanish is the sole official language nationwide, but Catalan (Catalonia/Valencia/Balearics), Basque (a language isolate unrelated to any other European language), and Galician (closely related to Portuguese) are co-official within their own autonomous communities — bilingual road signage there is a strong regional identifier.
